info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 105 hours self-study (including projects preparation)
info.prerequisite:
ENS411 & ENS421 & ENR401 & ENW401 & ENP101 & ENG301
K15 onward: Passed ERW411 & LTG202
info.description:
This course is designed to build and develop foundational translation skills for 3rd-year English majors, equipping students to confidently translate between English and Vietnamese in both directions. I
Students are expected to acquire and apply basic knowledge of theoretical aspects covering from translation methods, translating process, equivalence, and cultural issues... in their translation.
By applying the basic theoretical knowledge, students are expected to be able to efficiently handle compiled jobs in a classroom hypothetical environment, maintain and develop basic English language skills in accordance with translation of 4 main types of texts (C1 standard) including: narrative texts,descriptiom texts, discussion texts, and dialogues.
In response to the evolving demands of the language services industry, the course integrates the use of AI-based translation tools to help students become proficient in AI-assisted translation and post-editing.
info.studentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class
- Use their own laptop and tools in class and out of class ethically under the lecturer's instructions
- Read the textbook in advance

assessments.questionType:
Part A – Manual Translation: Students translate short texts in class (150–200 words) without AI.
Part B – AI Draft Translation: Use 1 AI tool to translate the same texts.
Part C – Reflection Report: compare human vs AI outputs, explain major errors corrected, and discuss what AI did better/ more poorly than humans.
assessments.knowledgeSkill: Human translation skills and AI critical exploration
assessments.note:
Part A: 70%
Part B and C: 30%

assessments.questionType:
Part A – AI Draft Generation: Students choose 2 culturally rich texts (1 in English and the other in Vietnamese) with teacher's approval and use AI to translate them.
Part B – Light cultural adaptation: Post-edit them for a specific target audience each text (e.g., American tourists, academic readers), submitting both AI's works and human's edited version.
Part C – Presentation: Short oral presentation (10 minutes) of outputs and reasoning.
assessments.knowledgeSkill: Human-in-the-loop editing, cultural literacy in translation and AI ethics
assessments.note:
Part A and B: 70%
Part C: 30%
